The  British Business Bank  (BBB) has acquired a £43m stake in  Oxford Science Enterprises (OSE), an independent investment company that helps turn University of Oxford research into startups.

The £43m investment marks the BBB’s first investment in OSE, as it looks to scale the UK’s university spinout ecosystem.

The UK state-owned BBB and OSE have previously co-invested in ten Oxford University spinouts, most recently AI chip startup Fractile, with OSE the first investor in Fractile. They have also co-invested in OMass Therapeutics, Quantum Motion, and Oxford Quantum Circuits.

European spinouts have raised $13.8bn so far in 2026, with OSE’s portfolio contributing $1.5bn in the first nine months.

The BBB said the partnership between the BBB and the OBE will deepen collaboration on future co-investments and give OSE’s portfolio companies greater access to the BBB’s long-term capital as they scale.

OSE, founded in 2015, is an independent investment company, which aims to turn University of Oxford research into startups. It works with academics to form companies and invests in areas including life sciences, healthtech and deeptech. The University of Oxford owns five per cent of OSE.

OSE has had two major exits behind it: quantum computing company Oxford Ionics was acquired by US-listed IonQ for $1.075bn last year and biotech firm Dark Blue Therapeutics was acquired by Amgen in a $840m deaf completed last year.

Leandros Kalisperas, Chief Investment Officer, the British Business Bank, said: “By working more closely with OSE, we aim to help high-potential spinouts to grow faster and ensure the UK benefits from the breakthroughs it creates.”

Ed Bussey, CEO of Oxford Science Enterprises, said: “OSE is emerging as the world’s largest venture builder of deep science companies dedicated to a single university – a flagship in an area in which the UK now leads the world, at a time of unparalleled need for stronger economic growth and national resilience.

“This investment is a hugely welcome endorsement of the strategic importance of OSE to the UK’s future prosperity, health and security and I’m looking forward to working closely with the British Business Bank to meaningfully improve all of these outcomes to the benefit of the whole of the UK.”
